parts.title: Scented Plants
parts.article:
A Many plants emit a smell. This may come from the flower of the plant, from the leaves, stem, or even, in some cases, from the root. What humans may perceive as a fragrant perfume is actually a tool used by plants to entice pollinators, discourage bacteria, or fend off predators. Fragrances consist of small organic particles with high vapor pressures, so that a scent compound evaporates easily if exposed to the air; chemicals which evaporate in this way are described as ‘volatile compounds’.

B Although we generally think of plant odors as pleasant, many volatile compounds in plants are toxic when eaten. These compounds are used by plants to protect themselves from bacterial attack. Humans have recognized and taken advantage of these plant-derived antibacterials since antiquity, when they were used to slow the spoilage of food. For example, the spice clove could be used in baked goods and prepared meats to slow the growth of mould and bacteria, because a small amount was not dangerous to humans. Before the development of modern food preservation techniques, European civilization was heavily dependent on cloves and other tropical spices to ensure a long-lasting supply of food. However, the long distance from Europe to South-east Asia made these spices extremely expensive and was part of the motivation behind the search for a shorter route to Asia, which resulted in the discovery of the Americas.

C Although volatile compounds in plants probably originally evolved to repel herbivorous (plant-eating) animals of all kinds, they now perform a remarkable range of functions. An important one common to many plants is to attract animals which will spread that plant’s pollen. Insects are the most common animals to interact with plants in this way, and most insects detect volatile compounds through the extremely sensitive antennae on their heads. Some antennae can detect an airborne volatile compound at concentrations of just a few parts per billion.

D Other plants emit volatile compounds which function as toxins against invading insects, and still others emit such compounds when they have been injured, in order to deter insects from laying eggs on them and thus injuring them further. Volatile compounds released by plants in response to herbivore egg-laying, for example, can attract parasites of the eggs, thereby preventing them from hatching. In this way the plant can avoid the attack of the hungry young herbivores that would have emerged from the eggs.

E Volatile compounds in plants can also be used as a kind of currency in some very indirect defensive systems. In the rainforest tree Leonardoxa africana, for example, ants of the species Petalomyrmex phylax are attracted to young leaves because they emit high levels of the volatile compound methyl salicylate, a substance that ants need to use as an antiseptic in their nests; coincidentally, the ants attack any herbivorous insects that they encounter. It appears that methyl salicylate both attracts ants and rewards them for performing their valuable role in deterring herbivores. The web of interactions among plants and animals can become so complicated that it is difficult to detect what the outcome of the release of volatile compounds is. But it is clear that the system can have a defensive purpose, as many experiments have shown that the deactivation of a plant’s volatile emission system makes it more vulnerable to herbivores.

F Floral scent has a strong impact on the economic success of many agricultural crops that rely on insect pollinators, including fruit trees such as the bee-pollinated cherry, apple, apricot, and peach, as well as vegetables and tropical plants such as the papaya. A decrease in fragrance emission, due to crossbreeding for fruit size or other characteristics, reduces the ability of plants to attract pollinators and may result in considerable losses for growers. This problem has been made worse in the United States by recent epidemics that have infected and killed many honeybees, the major insect pollinator.

G Some plant breeders have tried to solve this pollination problem by spraying scent compounds on orchard trees to enhance honeybee foraging, but this approach was costly and, in the end, proved to be inefficient. One of the reasons for its ineffectiveness was that general spraying of the crop could not tell insects exactly where the blossoms were. Clearly, a more refined strategy is needed; genetic manipulation of scents, for example, would allow growers to regulate the types of insect pollinators and the frequency of their visits.

H Such manipulation of scent will also benefit people who grow flowers commercially. Cut flowers and potted plants play an important aesthetic part in human life. Unfortunately, traditional breeding has produced varieties with improved vase life, color, and shape, while perfume has been sacrificed. The loss of scent among ornamental flowers, which have a worldwide annual value of more than US$30 billion, makes them important targets for the genetic manipulation of flower fragrance. Some preliminary experiments have already been carried out, but for technical reasons the scent was present in every part of the plant, rather than being localized in the flower, and the level of intensity of fragrance was below the threshold of detection for the human nose. The next generation of experiments, already in progress, will include more sophisticated schemes that target the expression of scent specifically to flowers or other organs, such as special glands that can store antibacterial or herbivore-repellent compounds.
parts.questions:
Questions 1–4
Reading Passage 1 has eight paragraphs, A-H.
Which paragraph contains the following information?
Write the correct letter, A-H, in boxes 1–4 on your answer sheet.

Q1 a list of food plants which need insects to make them productive

  • A
  • B
  • C
  • D
  • E
  • F
  • G
  • H

Q2 an explanation of why a genetic experiment may assist plant reproduction

Q3 a description of current research with advantages for the flower industry

Q4 an explanation of how insects perceive volatile compounds in plants

Questions 5–9
Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
Write the correct letter in boxes 5–9 on your answer sheet.

Q5 According to the passage, spices were used in the past to

  • A keep insects away from food.
  • B improve the taste of food.
  • C prevent the decay of food.
  • D make food smell more attractive.

Q6 The Leonardoxa africana tree protects itself by

  • A emitting a scent that repels plant-eating insects.
  • B attracting and poisoning herbivorous insects.
  • C chemically destroying the eggs of parasites.
  • D attracting an enemy of herbivorous insects.

Q7 Which of the following statements about methyl salicylate is NOT true according to the passage?

  • A It helps ants to protect their nests.
  • B It helps herbivorous insects to find food.
  • C It helps a rainforest tree to attract ants.
  • D It helps a rainforest tree to avoid being eaten.

Q8 Which factor has made the problems of US fruit growers more serious?

  • A Bees found an alternative source of food.
  • B Chemicals were killing too many bees.
  • C Fruit was decreasing in quality.
  • D Bees have had their numbers reduced by disease.

Q9 Experiments in genetically manipulating the fragrance of ornamental flowers have

  • A cost US$30 billion.
  • B made the flowers more attractive to insects.
  • C failed to produce a strong enough scent.
  • D reduced production on flower farms.
Questions 10–13
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 10–13 on your answer sheet, write.

Q10 The theory that plants defend themselves with smells is untested.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q11 The smell from fruit-tree flowers is important to farmers.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q12 The population of honeybees in Europe has declined.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q13 Applying perfume to orchard trees is accepted as a good method of increasing pollination.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

reference:
Q1

解析 F段列举了樱桃、苹果等需要蜜蜂传粉的水果和蔬菜，这直接对应了题干所要找的“需要昆虫才能高产的食用植物清单”。

干扰 你可能在其他段落也看到了昆虫或植物，但全篇只有F段给出了包含好几种作物的具体“清单（list）”。

句子 Floral scent has a strong impact on the economic success of many agricultural crops that rely on insect pollinators, including fruit trees such as the bee-pollinated cherry, apple, apricot, and peach, as well as vegetables and tropical plants such as the papaya.

Q2

解析 G段最后指出，通过基因技术改变气味，能让种植者控制传粉昆虫的种类和它们飞来的频率，这就解释了为什么基因实验能帮助植物更好地繁殖。

干扰 H段虽然也提到了基因操作（genetic manipulation），但那是为了提升鲜花产业的商业价值（让花变香），不是为了帮助“植物繁殖（plant reproduction）”。

句子 Clearly, a more refined strategy is needed; genetic manipulation of scents, for example, would allow growers to regulate the types of insect pollinators and the frequency of their visits.

Q3

解析 H段提到目前正在进行的新一代实验能更精准地只让花朵散发香味，这能解决观赏花卉没有香味的问题，从而极大地造福花卉产业。

干扰 你可能会在原文里死找“research（研究）”这个词，但原文用的是“already in progress（已经在进行中）”的“experiments（实验）”来进行同义替换。

句子 The loss of scent among ornamental flowers, which have a worldwide annual value of more than US$30 billion, makes them important targets for the genetic manipulation of flower fragrance. Some preliminary experiments have already been carried out... The next generation of experiments, already in progress, will include more sophisticated schemes that target the expression of scent specifically to flowers or other organs...

Q4

解析 C段明确说明了大多数昆虫是通过头上极其敏感的“触角（antennae）”来探测植物散发的气味的，解释了昆虫如何感知气味。

干扰 其他段落虽然大篇幅讲了植物气味能吸引或驱赶昆虫，但只有C段解释了昆虫到底是用什么生理器官来“感知（perceive）”这些气味的。

句子 Insects are the most common animals to interact with plants in this way, and most insects detect volatile compounds through the extremely sensitive antennae on their heads. Some antennae can detect an airborne volatile compound at concentrations of just a few parts per billion.

Q5

解析 原文B段清楚地指出，过去人们利用香料植物的抗菌特性来减缓食物变质（slow the spoilage of food），对应C选项的“防止食物腐烂（prevent the decay of food）”。

干扰 你可能受生活常识影响，觉得加香料是为了让食物更好吃（选项B）或更香（选项D），但原文强调它的核心作用是用来杀菌防腐。

句子 Humans have recognized and taken advantage of these plant-derived antibacterials since antiquity, when they were used to slow the spoilage of food. For example, the spice clove could be used in baked goods and prepared meats to slow the growth of mould and bacteria...

Q6

解析 原文E段写这种树通过散发气味吸引来蚂蚁，而蚂蚁作为“保镖”会攻击吃植物的昆虫，这对应了D选项的“吸引食草昆虫的敌人”。

干扰 你可能想选A或B，但这种树释放的气味本身并没有直接驱赶或毒死食草昆虫，它是靠招来能打架的蚂蚁来保护自己的。

句子 In the rainforest tree Leonardoxa africana, for example, ants of the species Petalomyrmex phylax are attracted to young leaves... coincidentally, the ants attack any herbivorous insects that they encounter. It appears that methyl salicylate both attracts ants and rewards them for performing their valuable role in deterring herbivores.

Q7

解析 原文说水杨酸甲酯（methyl salicylate）能吸引蚂蚁，并被蚂蚁拿回窝里当杀菌剂，从而保护树木免受食草昆虫的伤害；全文根本没提这东西能帮食草昆虫找食物，因此B选项的说法是错的。

干扰 做这种题极容易看漏题干里的“NOT TRUE（不正确）”，A、C、D选项都在原文里能找到对应的好处，只有B选项与原文逻辑完全相反。

句子 In the rainforest tree Leonardoxa africana, for example, ants of the species Petalomyrmex phylax are attracted to young leaves because they emit high levels of the volatile compound methyl salicylate, a substance that ants need to use as an antiseptic in their nests; coincidentally, the ants attack any herbivorous insects that they encounter.

Q8

解析 F段最后一句指出，美国最近发生的流行病（epidemics）感染并杀死了大量蜜蜂，导致水果种植者的问题更加严重，完全对应D选项的“疾病使蜜蜂数量减少”。

干扰 你可能会被B选项的“Chemicals（化学物质）”迷惑，但原文说的是传染病（epidemics）导致蜜蜂死亡，并没有提到是化学物质惹的祸。

句子 This problem has been made worse in the United States by recent epidemics that have infected and killed many honeybees, the major insect pollinator.

Q9

解析 H段提到初步的基因实验碰到了技术问题，导致花香的强度低于人类鼻子的检测门槛，意思就是香味太淡了闻不到，对应C选项的“未能产生足够强烈的气味”。

干扰 你可能会手滑选A，但原文的300亿美元（US$30 billion）指的是全世界观赏花卉一年的总商业价值，而不是这个实验花了多少钱。

句子 Some preliminary experiments have already been carried out, but for technical reasons the scent was present in every part of the plant, rather than being localized in the flower, and the level of intensity of fragrance was below the threshold of detection for the human nose.

Q10

解析 原文E段最后一句明确提到“许多实验已经证明（many experiments have shown）”植物确实靠气味系统防御，这与题干中说这个理论“未被测试（untested）”的意思完全相反。

干扰 题干里的“untested”是一个很绝对的否定词，只要你在原文读到了任何带有“实验（experiments）”或“证明”字眼的内容，就可以果断判错。

句子 But it is clear that the system can have a defensive purpose, as many experiments have shown that the deactivation of a plant’s volatile emission system makes it more vulnerable to herbivores.

Q11

解析 F段明确表示花香对许多农作物的经济成功有巨大影响，如果不香了会导致种植者面临巨大损失，这说明花香对农民来说当然非常重要。

干扰 虽然原文没有一字不差地写出“important to farmers”，但它用了“经济成功（economic success）”和“种植者的损失（losses for growers）”做了非常完美的同义替换。

句子 Floral scent has a strong impact on the economic success of many agricultural crops... A decrease in fragrance emission... reduces the ability of plants to attract pollinators and may result in considerable losses for growers.

Q12

解析 原文F段提到了美国（United States）的蜜蜂数量因疾病减少，但整篇文章从头到尾都没有提过“欧洲（Europe）”的蜜蜂数量到底有没有下降。

干扰 你可能看到原文写了蜜蜂大量死亡，就觉得题干说得对顺手选了TRUE，但做判断题一定要核对主语的限定条件，美国发生的事不能套在欧洲头上。

句子 This problem has been made worse in the United States by recent epidemics that have infected and killed many honeybees, the major insect pollinator.

Q13

解析 G段明确指出，给果树喷洒气味的方法不仅成本高，而且最终证明是“效率低下的（inefficient）”，这跟题干里说的“被认为是好方法（accepted as a good method）”截然相反。

干扰 你可能只读了前半句，看到有人确实尝试去果园喷香水解决问题，但忽略了后半句作者对这个方法直接给出了“又贵又没用（costly and inefficient）”的负面评价。

句子 Some plant breeders have tried to solve this pollination problem by spraying scent compounds on orchard trees to enhance honeybee foraging, but this approach was costly and, in the end, proved to be inefficient. One of the reasons for its ineffectiveness was that general spraying of the crop could not tell insects exactly where the blossoms were.
